Standalone Go archive/zip fixture, Go 1.25 Alpine. Standard library only; no BookStark Go build. Fixed timestamp, genuine signed data descriptors, UTF-8 attachment path, stored and deflated files plus a directory. Regenerate only in the isolated NAS test workspace, then copy the fixture here.

Generators use //go:build ignore so root module discovery never includes standalone main functions. Run explicitly with go run generate.go or go run generate_contract.go in an isolated output directory. Contract fixtures reflect models/export.go field names/types, use genuine Go json.Encoder and archive/zip, and contain synthetic values only. Protected contract envelopes are structure fixtures only; real crypto interoperability vectors live separately in tool/legacy_crypto_test.


Identity/mapping/storage fixtures are generated by generate_identities.go in a fresh isolated NAS output directory, using Go archive/zip and json.Decoder.UseNumber. They preserve int64 IDs, tuple aliases, optional child IDs, forward parents, explicit conflicts, structural protected records, and a multi-MiB Unicode/BOM/CRLF source. Check all previously published ZIP hashes before copying new variants. The structural dummy hashes/envelopes are NOT crypto interoperability vectors.
generate_time.go independently produces 25 synthetic vectors using Go time.Parse/UnixMilli (reference runtime go1.25.14); these cover UTC/offsets/nanoseconds/negative epoch/invalid calendars. The real Go/Android crypto vectors remain in tool/legacy_crypto_test.

Upload plan/copy/SQL fixtures add shared Unicode thumbnails, original-as-thumbnail, an explicit empty section, ambiguous percent paths and a 9,100,000-byte binary stream. Generated with standard-library Go1.25.14 in isolated outputs r10/r11; all preceding28 ZIP hashes remain unchanged in r11. These are synthetic contract samples, not user archives.

The current generate_identities.go invocation also requires the public tool/legacy_crypto_test/go-vectors.json catalog as a third command argument. r12 produced32 ZIPs using only Go standard-library JSON/archive tooling; old29 ZIP hashes are unchanged. New protected-native/Unicode/plaintext compatibility cases contain real synthetic Go bcrypt/GCM reference data, not dummy envelopes. These public test passwords are never production credentials.
